This page collects the **reading material** for the workshop. It splits into two layers:

- **Chapters 0–12** — the long-form prose treatment of the workshop's topics. Each chapter pairs **1:1** with a lecture and a tutorial. Read these as the "textbook" of the workshop.
- **Appendices A–K** — background reading on prerequisite skills (R, Unix, single-cell biology, statistics) and reference material the chapters cite into (computing fundamentals, shell scripting, Git, HPC/Talapas, databases, file formats, a methods-section template). Read what you need, when you need it.

## How to use these resources

::: callout-tip
**For the chapters and lectures:** read in numerical order, and each chapter *before* its tutorial.

**For the appendices:** read on demand. The chapters cross-reference the appendices liberally — when a chapter says "see Appendix D § 8 for why per-cell DE fails", that's a hint to read that section before continuing.

**Suggested initial reading order if you're new to the toolchain:** A (R) → B (Unix) → F (GREP & shell) → G (Git) → E (computing fundamentals) → H (Talapas/HPC). Read the *Glossary* alongside the lectures.

**If your molecular biology is rusty:** Appendix C, before Lecture 00.

**If your statistics is rusty:** Appendix D, before Lecture 05 / Chapter 5.

**Once you start writing up your own scRNA-seq results:** keep Appendix K (Methods-Section Template) open in another tab.
:::

For curated **single-cell tutorials, papers, and external references**, see [Additional Resources](Additional_Resources.qmd).
